title: Training Semi-Supervised Deep Learning Models with Heuristic Early Stopping Rules

raw.stage1:
### Purpose
The contribution aims to address the lack of objective methodology for determining when to stop training semi-supervised deep learning (SSDL) models, specifically to prevent overfitting and error propagation from noisy pseudo-labels, with a focus on healthcare/mHealth data. Paper [4] discusses early stopping methods that use unlabeled samples and confidence-based criteria to prevent overfitting, which aligns with the general objective of stopping training to avoid overfitting in semi-supervised learning. Paper [7] also addresses the issue of error propagation from noisy pseudo-labels in SSDL, focusing on confidence-based pseudo-label selection to mitigate classification errors. Both papers share the same problem-class level objective of improving SSDL training by addressing overfitting and noisy pseudo-labels.

### Mechanism
The contribution proposes three heuristic early-stopping criteria: (1) layer-wise weight-change stabilization, (2) minimizing validation cross-entropy loss, and (3) sliding-window confidence-based pseudo-label counting, combined via a ranking mechanism. Paper [2] introduces an early stopping criterion based on local gradient statistics, which is conceptually similar to layer-wise weight-change stabilization (criterion 1). Paper [4] proposes confidence-based early stopping using unlabeled samples, which aligns with criterion 3 (pseudo-label confidence). Paper [7] discusses confidence-based pseudo-label selection, which overlaps with criterion 3 as well. However, no prior paper combines these criteria into a ranking-based mechanism as described in the contribution.

### Evaluation
The evaluation uses subject-dependent longitudinal 4-fold cross-validation on mHealth clinical-trial data. Paper [7] evaluates confidence-based pseudo-label selection in SSDL using cross-validation, which matches the general evaluation design of validating pseudo-label-based methods in SSDL. Paper [4] also uses confidence-based early stopping methods validated on text classification datasets, which aligns with the evaluation design of testing early stopping criteria in SSDL. Both papers reuse standard evaluation designs (cross-validation and confidence-based validation) for similar claims, making the evaluation facet covered.

### Domain
The contribution applies semi-supervised deep learning to mHealth/digital-health prediction. Paper [26] applies semi-supervised learning to disease diagnosis from medical images, which falls within the broader healthcare domain. Paper [7] applies SSDL to tabular data, which is a general domain that includes healthcare applications. Both papers address semi-supervised learning in healthcare-related areas, making the domain facet covered.

## PURPOSE

The purpose is: provide an objective methodology for *when to stop training* SSDL models, specifically to prevent overfitting and error propagation from noisy pseudo-labels in healthcare/mHealth data with many missing labels.

Paper [4] proposes "an early stopping method that uses unlabeled samples" for semi-supervised settings, addressing overfitting in low-resource settings. Paper [11] evaluates "different early stopping rules (ESR) and their combinations for stopping the training of multi layer perceptrons." Paper [2] proposes "a novel early stopping criterion" to prevent poor generalization. However, none of these specifically target the SSDL (iterative pseudo-labeling loop) context where error propagation from noisy pseudo-labels is the core concern. Paper [4] is closest — it uses confidence of unlabeled samples for early stopping in semi-supervised text classification, which is substantively equivalent at the problem-class level: "when to stop training in a semi-supervised setting to prevent overfitting with noisy pseudo-labels." This is the same objective.

## MECHANISM

The three criteria are: (1) layer-wise weight-change (Euclidean norm) stabilization; (2) validation cross-entropy loss minimization; (3) sliding-window count of high-confidence pseudo-labels (probability > theta). Combined via rank aggregation.

- Criterion 2 (validation loss) is standard and covered by [9], [11], [2].
- Criterion 1 (weight-change norm) is covered by [2] ("local statistics of the computed gradients") and [11] (evaluates multiple ESRs including weight-based).
- Criterion 3 (confidence of pseudo-labels via threshold) is covered by [4] ("based on confidence and class...") and [7] ("confidence-based pseudo-labeling").
- Rank aggregation of multiple criteria is covered by [24] ("weighted rank aggregation to achieve multiple query criteria") and [29] (multi-criteria active learning with rank aggregation).

The combination of all three into a rank-aggregation framework for SSDL stopping is partially assembled from these pieces. Paper [11] explicitly evaluates "combinations" of early stopping rules for MLPs. Paper [24] uses rank aggregation for combining multiple criteria. The individual primitives are all present across prior work.

## EVALUATION

The evaluation design uses subject-dependent longitudinal 4-fold cross-validation on clinical trial mHealth data with a binary outcome. The CV design (k-fold cross-validation with subject-dependent splits) is a standard evaluation design used broadly. Paper [11] uses cross-validation for evaluating early stopping rules. The specific mHealth clinical trial dataset is unique, but the evaluation *design* (k-fold CV, binary classification metrics) is standard and covered by [11] and others.

## DOMAIN

The domain is semi-supervised deep learning for mHealth/digital-health prediction. Paper [26] applies semi-supervised learning to medical images. Paper [5] reviews SSL across application domains including healthcare. However, mHealth/digital-health with wearable sensor data for clinical trial compliance is a specific sub-area. Paper [26] covers medical image diagnosis. The general area of "semi-supervised learning for healthcare" is present in [26] and [5], making this COVERED as a sub-instance of healthcare ML.
